newsitem.title: USA: PP&L sees Pa. nuke at full output Thursday.
newsitem.headline: PP&L sees Pa. nuke at full output Thursday.

text.p: Pennsylvania Power and Light Co (PP&L) said Tuesday its 1,090 megawatt (MW) Susquehanna 1 nuclear unit is expected to resume full production Thursday after being restarted late Monday.
"We started it up late last evening. One hundred percent (power) will be on Thursday," said an onsite plant spokesman. "There's a ramping curve they follow."
Susquehanna 1 was shut Feb 25 in anticipation of a loss of vacuum in its main condenser. Its restart was delayed for additional repairs.
The unit reached approximately 40 percent power this morning, the spokesman said.
The adjacent 1,094 MW Susquehanna unit 2 was shut last Saturday for planned refueling and maintenance. The outage would last about six weeks.

The Susquehanna units in Berwick, Pa., are jointly owned by PP&L and Allegheny Electric Cooperative. They account for 30 percent of PP&L's power deliveries and 20 percent of its installed generation capacity.
